lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush's ecstatic welcome when Elizabeth returned — the dog who would follow them to Pisa.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Robert admits he sometimes shortened visits just to reach the moment of taking her hand.

lines.text: How I wish for two hearts to love you with, and two lives to give to you, and two souls to bear the weight worthily of all you have given to me.
lines.note: Elizabeth wishes for two hearts and two lives to give him — the depth of her devotion early on.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: The shock of losing Flush in the street — a crisis that drew them together.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Elizabeth's witty resolution of the Flush debate: 'I am your Flush, and he is mine.'

lines.text: But I seem really to grow under you,—my faculties extend toward yours.
lines.note: Robert feels he grows under her — his faculties extending toward hers.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Flush found again, lying on the sofa with paw and ears hanging over — the ransom paid.

lines.text: May God bless you—‘and me in you.’
lines.note: Elizabeth blesses him 'and me in you' — love so complete it names itself inside him.

lines.text: Also I will ever say, God bless you, my dearest dearest,—my perfect angel you have been!
lines.note: Robert calls her his 'perfect angel' across nearly two years without a blank.

lines.text: I was yours long ago, and though you give me back my promise at this eleventh hour, ... you generous, dear unkind! ... you know very well that you can do as well without it.
lines.note: She was his long ago — even if he gave back her promise at the eleventh hour.

lines.text: All that I am, I owe you—if I enjoy anything now and henceforth, it is through you.
lines.note: After the wedding she writes that all she is, she owes him.

lines.text: You take my words from me—I ‘exult’ in the irrevocability of this precious bestowal of yourself on me—come what will my life has borne flower and fruit—it is a glorious, successful, felicitous life, I thank God and you.
lines.note: Robert exults that his life has borne flower and fruit — a glorious, felicitous life.

lines.text: By to-morrow at this time, I shall have you only, to love me—my beloved!
lines.note: On the eve of departure: by to-morrow at this time she shall have him only.

lines.text: I begin to think that none are so bold as the timid, when they are fairly roused.
lines.note: Her final reflection — none are so bold as the timid, when fairly roused.
